Definition: of Hebrew origin (H7014); Cain, (i.e. Cajin), the son of Adam:--Cain.
BiblicalUsage: Cain is the first murderer, the son of Adam who killed his brother Abel and then went out from the presence of the LORD. Hebrews remembers Abel's better sacrifice, John says Cain was of that wicked one and slew his brother because his own works were evil, and Jude warns of those who have gone in the way of Cain.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Cain is the first picture of what sin does when it is not mastered: it starts with a rejected offering and ends with a brother's blood. The way of Cain is still open, and the only way out of it is the better sacrifice Abel offered by faith.
